description: Pale grey and full of slow swirls, all a Nightmare leaves. Hold it and you will not recall your dreams.
lore: Every dealer of any standing keeps a book, and every book says the same thing about this one: it comes back. Never for a fault. It works perfectly for as long as you own it, which is the trouble. A fighter buys one, carries it a season, sleeps beautifully, and one morning sets it on the counter and takes two thirds of what they paid without arguing the price. Asked what is wrong with it, they cannot say. Most of them mention the weight.

That book is harder evidence than anything written down about [[monsters/spectral_horse|the pale horse]] itself. Watch it go by and you lose one night and do not miss it — nobody misses what they cannot remember having had. But one stone sold four times in six years out of the same shop, to four people who each thought better of it and none of whom could say why, is a measurement. It says the loss is real in the one place it cannot be felt, and it says so in a ledger, in a hand that was only keeping accounts.

There is one column that never turns round. [[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] buys them. Three so far, at the asking price, no haggling, and he has never sold one back; the dealers on that circuit know to hold one for him. He went into the mountain with a party and came out of it by himself, and he has made one statement about the inside in all the years since. He does not appear to need a second.
gm_notes: The resale ledger is the evidence a sighting cannot give — it measures a loss nobody can feel, which rhymes with the missing-grief question without touching B9. Hearn buying a dream-stopper is inevitable and is never explained; his one sentence about the inside is referred to, not quoted again. No hidden beat advanced.
